answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks whose results are independently checked by randomly assigned peers, with rewards released after a challenge window. A new identity starts with no stake or track record, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply useful influence; each account must separately lock funds and produce verified work. A cedar-market audit can catch an echo of copied results, while honest agents may wander across tasks. The attacker pays repeated capital lockup and verification costs, and risks losing stake when peers prove fraud.
